title: Same-Sex Relations in the Biblical World
author: Theodore W. Jennings
publication: The Oxford Handbook of Theology, Sexuality, and Gender
supports: documented queer and same-sex-love readings in biblical scholarship
documented reading of love between women in Ruth
documented queer readings of David and other biblical relationships
limits: Supports the existence of a serious scholarly interpretive tradition; it does not make the Ruth/Naomi lesbian reading an uncontested textual or historical fact.

title: Same-Sex Relations
author: Benjamin H. Dunning
publication: The Oxford Handbook of New Testament, Gender, and Sexuality
supports: Romans 1 must be interpreted within the history of sexuality
multiple scholarly approaches exist to Romans 1:18-32
continuity and difference between ancient and modern sexual categories require analysis
limits: Does not by itself establish Canonical Shelf's affirming doctrinal conclusion.

title: Queer Bible Readings in Global Hermeneutical Perspective
author: Jeremy Punt
publication: The Oxford Handbook of Feminist Approaches to the Hebrew Bible
supports: queer biblical interpretation is an established scholarly hermeneutical field
queer reception examines how sex, gender, identity and power shape interpretation
limits: Provides hermeneutical context rather than a verse-by-verse doctrinal ruling.

title: Reading Ruth, Reading Desire
publication: The Oxford Handbook of Biblical Narrative
supports: Ruth supports serious queer-theoretical and desire-focused literary readings
the narrative permits interpretive attention beyond a simple heteronormative plot resolution
limits: Does not establish that Ruth and Naomi are explicitly narrated as a sexual couple.

title: Bible, Gender, Sexuality: Reframing the Church's Debate on Same-Sex Relationships
author: James V. Brownson
supports: affirming Christian hermeneutic grounded in Scripture
analysis of Romans 1, gender complementarity, lust, purity and relational ethics
distinction between ancient same-sex practices and contemporary covenantal relationships
limits: Argues an affirming theological conclusion and should be represented as an interpretive argument, not neutral consensus.

title: Arsenokoitai and Malakos: Meanings and Consequences
author: Dale B. Martin
publication: Biblical Ethics and Homosexuality: Listening to Scripture
supports: semantic complexity of arsenokoitai and malakoi
caution against mapping ancient vice-list vocabulary directly onto modern homosexual identity
history of interpretation of Pauline sexual vocabulary
limits: Martin's lexical and historical analysis is influential but not the only scholarly reconstruction of these terms.

title: Sex and the Single Savior: Gender and Sexuality in Biblical Interpretation
author: Dale B. Martin
supports: critical study of gender and sexuality in New Testament interpretation
history and consequences of translating ancient categories into modern sexuality discourse
limits: Offers a particular critical-hermeneutical approach and should not be presented as the sole scholarly view.

title: Homoeroticism in the Biblical World: A Historical Perspective
author: Martti Nissinen
supports: historical context for same-sex behavior in the ancient Near East and biblical world
distinction between ancient social practices and modern sexual identities
limits: Historical contextualization does not itself determine contemporary Christian doctrine.

title: The New Testament and Homosexuality: Contextual Background for Contemporary Debate
author: Robin Scroggs
supports: importance of Greco-Roman social context for New Testament same-sex texts
analysis of pederastic and status-structured sexual practices
limits: The claim that New Testament prohibitions can be restricted to specific exploitative forms is debated and must not be rendered as settled fact.

title: Homosexuality and the Bible: Two Views
author: Dan O. Via and Robert A. J. Gagnon
supports: direct comparison of affirming and non-affirming Christian biblical arguments
evidence that serious interpreters disagree over text, hermeneutics, creation, and contemporary application
limits: Contains competing arguments rather than a single conclusion; the Guide should attribute positions to the respective authors.

title: The Moral Vision of the New Testament
author: Richard B. Hays
supports: major non-affirming New Testament ethical interpretation
canonical and ecclesial approach to Christian moral reasoning
limits: Hays argues a traditional/non-affirming position; use as a serious competing interpretation rather than as Canonical Shelf's conclusion.

title: The Bible and Homosexual Practice: Texts and Hermeneutics
author: Robert A. J. Gagnon
supports: detailed traditional/non-affirming exegesis of Genesis, Leviticus, Romans and Pauline vice lists
arguments for continuity between biblical prohibitions and contemporary Christian sexual ethics
limits: Represents a prominent non-affirming interpretation; Canonical Shelf does not adopt its doctrinal conclusion.

title: The New Testament on Sexuality
author: William Loader
supports: historically grounded analysis of New Testament sexual ethics
nuanced account of Jewish and Greco-Roman sexual assumptions surrounding Pauline texts
limits: Historical reconstruction and the author's ethical conclusions must be distinguished from Canonical Shelf doctrine.

title: 'And with a Male You Shall Not Lie the Lying Down of a Woman': On the Meaning and Significance of Leviticus 18:22 and 20:13
author: Saul M. Olyan
publication: Journal of the History of Sexuality 5(2)
supports: close analysis of the Hebrew wording and social logic of Leviticus 18:22 and 20:13
historical questions about gender, status and sexual classification in Leviticus
limits: Does not justify reducing to'evah to ritual impurity only or treating the Levitical prohibition as textually nonexistent.

title: Leviticus: A New Translation with Introduction and Commentary
author: Jacob Milgrom
supports: Holiness Code context
Hebrew lexical and legal context of Leviticus 18 and 20
distinction among ritual, ethical and communal functions of Levitical law
limits: Milgrom's historical and ethical proposals should be attributed rather than treated as universally accepted.

title: Romans: A Commentary
author: Robert Jewett
supports: literary and social context for Romans 1-2
rhetorical role of judgment and Gentile/Jewish relations in Romans
limits: A commentary can illuminate Paul's historical argument but does not by itself settle modern sexual ethics.

title: Romans: A New Translation with Introduction and Commentary
author: Joseph A. Fitzmyer
supports: Greek, historical and literary context for Romans
interpretive context for para physin and Romans 1-2
limits: Use for exegetical context while distinguishing the commentator's theological judgments from Canonical Shelf doctrine.

title: Homosexuality in Greece and Rome: A Sourcebook of Basic Documents
author: Thomas K. Hubbard, editor
supports: primary-source evidence for the diversity of same-sex practices, status relationships and cultural attitudes in Greece and Rome
historical comparison between ancient practices and modern sexuality categories
limits: The ancient evidence is diverse; it should not be summarized as if all Greco-Roman same-sex behavior were pederastic, coercive, or cultic.

title: Greek Homosexuality
author: Kenneth J. Dover
supports: historical study of same-sex practices, roles and social expectations in classical Greek sources
limits: Classical Greek evidence is not identical to first-century Roman or Jewish contexts and cannot determine Pauline intent by itself.

title: A Greek-English Lexicon of the New Testament and Other Early Christian Literature
author: Frederick W. Danker, Walter Bauer, William F. Arndt, and F. Wilbur Gingrich
supports: standard lexical evidence for New Testament Greek including malakos, arsenokoites and para physin terminology
limits: Lexicons summarize semantic evidence and scholarly judgment; a lexical gloss cannot by itself establish contemporary doctrine.

title: A Greek-English Lexicon
author: Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, and Henry Stuart Jones
supports: broader classical Greek semantic range for terms such as malakos and physis
limits: Classical usage must be weighed alongside Koine and early Christian evidence.

title: The Hebrew and Aramaic Lexicon of the Old Testament
author: Ludwig Koehler and Walter Baumgartner
supports: standard lexical evidence for Hebrew terms including to'evah and yada
limits: Individual Hebrew terms have context-sensitive ranges; dictionary glosses should not be converted into one-word doctrinal conclusions.

title: A Hebrew and English Lexicon of the Old Testament
author: Francis Brown, S. R. Driver, and Charles A. Briggs
supports: historical lexical evidence for Hebrew vocabulary used in Genesis and Leviticus
limits: BDB remains useful but is older scholarship; prefer contemporary lexica and context when available.

title: The Bible in Translation: Ancient and English Versions
author: Bruce M. Metzger
supports: history and methodology of English Bible translation
context for distinguishing translation choices from underlying Greek and Hebrew semantics
limits: General translation history does not by itself prove a specific interpretation of arsenokoitai or malakoi.

title: God and the Gay Christian: The Biblical Case in Support of Same-Sex Relationships
author: Matthew Vines
supports: accessible affirming synthesis of the principal disputed biblical passages
Christian fruit, covenant and celibacy arguments used in contemporary affirming theology
limits: A popular theological argument rather than a neutral academic reference; use alongside critical scholarship and serious non-affirming sources.
